The change is documentation only: freshness anchoring of performance observations (head ~619-625), and a deadline admission estimator description with a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback (head ~869-905). The patch excerpt is truncated and the new head text is not visible, so I could not inspect the new documentation content. No code, crypto, authorization, attestation or key-handling files changed in the visible scope.

Relevant security-adjacent content examined: the prefix-cache description (T-041, unchanged), MTP typical-acceptance (approximate output, described as non-distribution-exact, not a trust-boundary change), and the media caps and decode-memory accounting (T-050 area, unchanged). The doc says the deadline catalog is empty and estimator changes touch only admission timing and availability. They do not alter A-001 confidentiality, T-053 authorization binding, or T-041 cache scope, TTL or HMAC naming.

I identified no concrete regression or invalidated threat assumption. Remaining uncertainty: the code behind the described estimator changes (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate) is not supplied. An incorrect admission estimate could affect availability (admitting overloaded work) but this is not evidenced here. The integration pass should check that code if it is included in other batches. The documented DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES env var is a performance-affecting setting, and the existing guard (DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification rejecting unrecognized DARKBLOOM_*) should be checked to confirm it covers this new key.
